key_insight: By combining photoluminescence imaging with drift-diffusion modeling and Bayesian inference, the study identifies where perovskite solar cell degradation starts and shows that the dominant failures are often localized at the transport-layer interfaces rather than uniformly in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: The workflow provides a diagnostic tool for mapping device aging mechanisms, helping engineers target interface passivation and fabrication changes to improve perovskite solar cell durability.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to microscopic observations
Bayesian inference used to generate spatial maps of recombination-related parameters over aging time
evidence_signal: The authors tracked inferred parameter maps during accelerated aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed strong spatially non-uniform degradation, with the largest changes concentrated near perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred mechanism maps depend on model assumptions and imaging quality, so mis-specified drift-diffusion priors or limited spatial resolution could affect how precisely degradation is attributed.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
